scene.note: The page's look is spread over forty style attributes in index.html, and by the end it lives in styles.css alone, where one colour is one edit.

steps.note: Ruth wants a warmer cream to match the new signs. Today that one colour is typed again and again across index.html.
Search index.html for style attributes. Each one styles a single element and nothing else.
Move every declaration into styles.css. Add a class where you need a hook, or use a selector for an element that is already there.
When index.html has no style attribute and no style element left, the page still looks exactly as it did.
styles.css now holds every rule, but the same colours are still written out in many of them.
Give the page's colours names as custom properties on :root. Pick the names yourself.
Every other rule uses a name instead of spelling out a colour, so each colour value is written once.
Do the same for the page's spacing, and use at least one of those names in a padding, a margin or a gap.
Next time Ruth asks for a new cream, it is one edit and every part of the page follows.
In each event card the date should be green and the description grey.
Two rules in styles.css both reach the date, and the dates only come out green because of !important.
Take the !important out and the date turns grey. Change the selectors so the right rule wins on its own.
With no !important anywhere, every date is green again and every description is still grey.
